name: Grumium
description: A star 35 parsecs away, 11 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 87585: radius 11.456 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 49.26 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 87585: effective temperature 4521 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.071)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 87585: distance 34.507 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.004), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 35 parsecs away, 11 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 49 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,521 K, so 11.456 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 87585: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Xi Draconis
quotes.card: Xi Draconis is a double or binary star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Draco.
quotes.introduction: It has an apparent visual magnitude of 3.75.
